short: The black day of the German Army, and the largest tank attack of the war.
full:
Rawlinson's Fourth Army attacked east of Amiens at 4.20 a.m. on 8 August 1918 with the Canadian and Australian Corps leading, the French First Army on the right, and more than 500 tanks: Mark Vs and lengthened Mark V*s with the infantry, ninety-six Whippets and armoured cars to work the depth. As at Cambrai there was no preliminary bombardment, and the assembly had been concealed by wireless silence, night moves and aircraft flying to mask engine noise. The advance went up to eight miles on the first day and took nearly 30,000 prisoners.

Erich Ludendorff called 8 August the black day of the German Army, not for the ground lost but because units surrendered readily and reserves coming up were jeered at for prolonging the war. The tanks wore out fast — of the force committed, only a handful were still running by 12 August — and the offensive was shut down rather than pushed. It opened the Hundred Days, the continuous Allied advance that ended in the armistice three months later.
